text: Some watchers, however. <break time="0.8s" /> Were careless about their duty. <break time="0.8s" /> And they would deliberately huddle together. <break time="0.8s" /> In a distant corner over a game of cards. <break time="0.8s" /> Plainly intending to allow him. <break time="0.8s" /> A little refreshment. <break time="0.8s" /> Which they imagined he kept hidden somewhere. <break time="0.8s" /> Nothing tormented him more. <break time="0.8s" /> Than such watchers. <break time="0.8s" /> And sometimes. <break time="0.8s" /> Overcoming his weakness. <break time="0.8s" /> He sang for as long as he could during their watch. <break time="0.8s" /> Merely to show them. <break time="0.8s" /> How unjust their suspicion was. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet his singing did little good. <break time="0.8s" /> Since the watchers only marveled at the cleverness. <break time="0.8s" /> That allowed him. <break time="0.8s" /> As they believed. <break time="0.8s" /> To eat in secret. <break time="0.8s" /> Even while he sang. <break time="0.8s" /> Far more welcome to him. <break time="0.8s" /> Were the watchers. <break time="0.8s" /> Who sat close to the bars. <break time="0.8s" /> And, not satisfied with the dim lighting of the hall. <break time="0.8s" /> Shone on him the electric torches. <break time="0.8s" /> Supplied by the impresario. <break time="0.8s" /> The harsh light did not trouble him at all. <break time="0.8s" /> Since he could always doze a little anyway. <break time="0.8s" /> And he gladly spent whole nights. <break time="0.8s" /> Telling such watchers tales. <break time="0.8s" /> Of his wandering life. <break time="0.8s" /> And listening to theirs in turn. <break time="0.8s" /> In the morning he was happiest. <break time="0.8s" /> For then an enormous breakfast. <break time="0.8s" /> Was brought to them. <break time="0.8s" /> At his own expense. <break time="0.8s" /> And they fell upon it. <break time="0.8s" /> With the healthy appetite of men. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had spent a long, sleepless night. <break time="0.8s" /> Since no one could watch him. <break time="0.8s" /> Every minute of every day. <break time="0.8s" /> No one but the artist himself could know. <break time="0.8s" /> Whether his fast had truly been unbroken. <break time="0.8s" /> And he alone, therefore. <break time="0.8s" /> Could be its fully satisfied spectator. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet he was never satisfied. <break time="0.8s" /> And perhaps it was not fasting at all. <break time="0.8s" /> That had made him so terribly thin. <break time="0.8s" /> But his own dissatisfaction. <break time="0.8s" /> For he alone knew. <break time="0.8s" /> What even the experts did not namely how easy fasting was.
